item.content:encoded:
Minor nitpick: saying just "11:42 AM" is not enough to describe the state of a sundial. Due to the way the Earth rotates around its axis and orbits the Sun accuracy of such devices varies continuously, requiring both date and time to identify a reading unambiguously. Moreover, given that sundials know nothing about time zones and simply measure local solar time, one should either specify the longitude difference between the device's position and the standard meridian (yes, even if UTC is used)… Personally, I would just avoid the issue altogether by replacing the time with "during testing", "in containment" or something equally vague, if not have the picture caption say "SCP-961" and nothing else.

That said, I like this article regardless and have been happy to upvote it.

item.content:encoded: This is one case where reflection on the entire entry feels larger than the sum of its parts. A device that displays history is one thing, to take it to a place where that history is inaccurate (maybe) is a totally different one, and I feel like you only start to play that angle at the very end in the entity description and recovery report. Further description and detail would make things clearer, but clear on the road to weirdness and not "over-analyzed". I'm interested to see the future of this entry.
